title: Is organic food really better for you?
summary: Student explainer weighing organic food: fewer pesticides and some higher nutrients, against higher cost, lower yields, honor-system certification and no proven health benefit.

assertions.quote: a certification process mainly relies on the honor system rather than on strength laboratory testing
they may not have an incentive to penalize clients who are going against the rules
being certified organic may not mean the product is truly organic
organic food contains higher levels of vitamin C iron phosphorus magnesium antioxidant activity and omega-3 fatty acids
organic food has lower levels of pesticide residues
no significant long-term health benefits have been found thus far
some organic products can cost up to 40% more than non-organic products
can have a yield up to 20% smaller
the lack of genetic modification causes organic food to spoil faster

verdicts.note: Few GM crops are engineered for shelf life, and studies find no consistent shelf-life difference attributable to organic production.
